title: Creation’s praise and why prayer is still required (chs. 7–8)
english: Even at sunrise there is something of the sun “upon us,” and creation’s praise does not cancel ours. It is not unreasonable to urge prayer by such examples: [[the heavens declare the glory of God >> Bible:Psalm 19:1]], yet we are still required to ask, lest neglect of prayer leave us without what God gives to those who seek.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 3 De oratione (OCR); no O’Meara/Greer/Chadwick wording.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Ask heavenly things; pray to the Father; toward the Lord’s Prayer (chs. 9–18)
english: Scripture trains us to ask for the great and heavenly things, to [[pray to the Father >> Bible:Matthew 6:9]] and not to any creature, and to offer one prayer to God through Christ. With that said, we turn to the prayer the Lord taught.
